name: AIGlassThemeProvider

screenshots.visual_note: Desktop mean luminance 242/255, std 18, ~20% non-bg: a pale white card stack on white; the visible content is story-authored inline-styled markup, not anything the provider generates.

material_impl: Provider renders a wrapper div with class glass-neutral-level1 plus hard-coded inline boxShadow 'rgba(15,23,42,0.10)...inset rgba(255,255,255,0.14)' (L511-517). Generated themes are HSL strings that are never applied to any CSS variable or ThemeProvider, so the 'theme' has no visual effect.
motion: None. useReducedMotion imported (L6) and never called; ANIMATION used only for a fake setTimeout delay.
a11y: No semantics needed for a provider, but it injects a visual wrapper div around app children (layout side-effect). 'accessibilityFirst'/'accessibilityMode' flags exist but are never read.
api: Function component, no forwardRef; className/data-testid only, no style passthrough. Context API is broad (16 members), with many no-op config flags (adaptToSeason, adaptToTime, enableABTesting, performanceMode duplicated as both config and state).
ssr: 'use client'. localStorage only inside effects (safe). Persists on every state change, including on mount, overwriting storage before the load effect's setState lands.
fake_complexity: Fake. generateTheme = setTimeout(ANIMATION.DURATION.slow) then Math.random() hue unless content contains 'urgent|important|breaking' (L289-301). 'sentiment', 'season', 'behavior' adaptation are not implemented. generateThemeFromSentiment builds a mock sentence and feeds it back in (L361-363).
target: src/theme/ThemeProvider (if any adaptive behavior is wanted, add a real token-mapping API there)
justification: The provider is labeled 'AI', but it picks a random hue after a fake delay, and the theme it produces is never connected to the token system, so nothing on screen changes. It also wraps consumer children in a decorated div, which a provider should never do. It is exported from the root, so removing it is a breaking change. Deprecate it in 4.x and remove it in 5.0. Adaptive theming belongs in the real ThemeProvider and token pipeline.

motion: All use the pattern initial={{opacity:0,...}} + animate={prefersReducedMotion ? {} : {...}}. justification: These are weaker, inaccessible clones of first-class components. Under reduced motion they become invisible: the modal blocks the page with nothing visible, and accordion and tab content never appears. Delete them from the GlassTransitions namespace.

material_impl: None (wrapper). The shimmer pattern animates the background shorthand between gradients, which overrides any glass surface background on the wrapped element.
motion: framer-motion useAnimation plus springs. Reduced motion is NOT wired: prefersReducedMotion is assigned (L366) and never read, so the breathe/drift/pulse infinite loops run for users who asked for reduced motion. The auto-trigger effect depends on executeSequence, which depends on activeSequences.size (L596-619); every start and finish changes size, which re-fires the effect and schedules duplicate sequences on top of the loop rescheduling (L567-581), compounding timers. Also attaches a window scroll listener that fires sequences on every scroll event (L709-723) without throttling.
a11y: The root has onClick/whileTap with no role or keyboard. 'Emotional context' drives motion intensity with no user control. The debug HUD has glass-focus/glass-touch-target classes on a pointer-events:none div (L748).
api: React.FC, no ref, no style; className via a string template. Props like performanceLevel, enableAdaptiveSpeed (UA sniffing, L464-479) and emotionalContext are pseudo-features. Not a root export, but reachable through the root export EnhancedGlassButton (src/components/button/EnhancedGlassButton.tsx:30, :424; src/index.ts:637).

fake_complexity: Fake framing. 'Physics simulation' (viscosity, elasticity, gravity unused), 'emotional context' (a table of springs) and 'adaptive speed' (UA regex). Under the branding it is a looped framer keyframe player.
target: framer-motion variants + motion tokens; EnhancedGlassButton should use a reduced-motion-aware hover/press primitive

name: ARGlassEffects (R3F implementation)
material_impl: Shader materials from ARGlassEffects.helpers (createSpatialUI, createHolographicGlass, createDataVisualization). A material is rebuilt via useMemo on every hover toggle (L647-657, L792-800) and never disposed, so GPU objects leak.
motion: useFrame loops. materialRef is never attached to the mesh in FloatingPanel/HolographicPortal (refs declared L639/L786, not passed), so `if (!materialRef.current) return` (L660, L803) exits every frame: no floating, rotation or uniform updates ever run. FloatingPanel calls setDistance in useFrame (L668), which would cause React re-renders per frame per panel if reached. Reduced motion is not applied inside the canvas.
a11y: Canvas-only interactive content (panels and portal are clickable meshes) with no DOM equivalent or labels. The capability list relies on emoji ✅/❌ with Tailwind text-green-400 classes that are not shipped.
api: Function, untyped internals (`: any` props on every sub-component). handlePortalActivation calls useReducedMotion() INSIDE a useCallback (L325-331): a Rules-of-Hooks violation that throws 'Invalid hook call' when the portal is clicked.
ssr: Imports three, @react-three/fiber and drei at module top. Correctly isolated behind the lazy wrapper and the aura-glass/three subpath.
fake_complexity: Fake. The code self-describes as 'Mock WebXR hook for demonstration' (L26). startARSession is a 1s timeout (L76-87); hit test and hand tracking return hard-coded vectors and fire 'surface_detected'/'hand_interaction' on mount (L105-149, L303-314); voice recognition is a no-op (L151-157); physics is empty (L557-572).
justification: This is a mock WebXR experience. It fires fake interaction events, never animates (unattached material refs), leaks materials, and crashes on portal click through a hook called inside a callback. It is the opposite of production 'Liquid Glass'. Remove it. If spatial work continues, start from a real WebXR session hook in a lab package.
